mainEntity.name: Why do metal building offices in the Cottonwood area struggle with sound control between rooms?

acceptedAnswer.text: Commercial facilities in Cottonwood and Camp Verde frequently utilize pre-engineered metal buildings with high metal roof decks that create massive shared ceiling plenums. When interior office partition walls stop at a standard 9-foot acoustic drop ceiling, sound travels straight over the wall, bounces off the metal roof decking, and drops into neighboring offices. Upgrades in these structures specifically require full-height drywall barriers or mass-loaded vinyl plenum curtains extended directly to the metal deck to achieve genuine speech privacy.
acceptedAnswer.description: Metal buildings often feature open roof plenums above drop ceilings, allowing sound to bypass short partition walls unless full-height barriers are installed to the deck.
